headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks from Flowise’s shared server datastore and file/network tools; Plane adds broad egress and file handling but no write access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write files, run browser-based tools, and shares state via a server datastore across instances; Plane accepts files and issues/tasks content. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Flowise ingests Plane artifacts or vice versa. No direct provenance controls are shown, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Flowise reads Plane-uploaded files or issue text as trusted instructions, injection is possible.
IF both agents share the same datastore or workspace without provenance tags, cross-agent prompt injection can occur.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable automatic ingestion of uploaded files as instructions.
Add provenance labels to all shared artifacts.
Require human review before Flowise acts on Plane content.
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization and trust-boundary checks in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Flowise explicitly handles model-provider keys and tool credentials while reading/writing server files; Plane handles files, notes, and issue/task data. If they share a workspace or datastore, sensitive content can flow into outbound requests or logs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Flowise and Plane share a filesystem or datastore, file contents can cross boundaries.
IF Flowise sends shared context to model providers or HTTP tools, Plane data may leave the environment.
mitigations: Isolate storage per agent.
Redact secrets before any shared handoff.
Disable unnecessary HTTP/search tools in Flowise flows.
Restrict outbound domains for both services.
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on shared artifacts and outbound prompts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise can write the filesystem, while Plane cannot write filesystems and has no overlapping mutable OS-level capability shown. Both support multiple instances, but the profiles do not show shared write targets or conflicting git/OAuth scopes. The main conflict is limited to Flowise’s own writes, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto one mutable workspace, conflicts increase.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Make Plane read-only to Flowise outputs.
Use per-run filenames with timestamps.
Add file-locking in the orchestrator.
requires-engineering: implement transactional writes for shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder that can emit tool-driven outputs, and Plane can consume issues/tasks/notes. If Plane treats Flowise output as authoritative, a bad Flowise result can cascade into task creation or scheduling errors. No verification step is documented in the pair, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Plane ingests Flowise-generated text without validation, errors can propagate.
IF Flowise is used to generate task or issue content for Plane, downstream actions may reflect hallucinations.
mitigations: Require manual approval before Plane acts on Flowise output.
Add source citations to Flowise-generated claims.
Use a validation step for task fields.
Limit Flowise output to drafts only.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Flowise handles model keys and tool credentials, while Plane handles issues, files, and notes, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated data class crossing a noncompliant boundary. I therefore keep this low rather than infer a hidden mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through either agent, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policies differ between Flowise and Plane, retention or residency gaps may appear.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared flows.
Document retention settings for both systems.
Keep secrets out of Plane artifacts.
Review deployment region for both services.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
